extra.message: The 'id' request parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL query "SELECT id, username, name, surname FROM users WHERE id=" + params["id"] and passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. UNION/boolean/time-based) to read the entire users table including passwords.

The 'v' request parameter is substituted via string formatting into the HTML response inside re.sub(), with no output encoding. Reflected user input lands in the HTML body, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution (reflected XSS).

The 'object' request parameter is base64/url-decoded and passed directly to pickle.loads(). Untrusted pickle data can execute arbitrary code via the __reduce__ protocol, resulting in remote code execution (insecure deserialization).

The 'path' request parameter is passed to open(os.path.abspath(params["path"]), "rb") without any allowlist or path canonicalization. os.path.abspath does not prevent '..' traversal, so an attacker can read arbitrary files on the server (local file inclusion / path traversal).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: When the 'path' parameter contains '://', urllib.request.urlopen(params["path"]) fetches an attacker-controlled URL. This enables Server-Side Request Forgery against internal services and cloud metadata endpoints, and the response is returned to the attacker.

The 'domain' request parameter is concatenated into a shell command "nslookup " + params["domain"] that is executed with subprocess.run(..., shell=True). Shell metacharacters (e.g. ';', '|', '`') allow arbitrary OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The 'xml' request parameter is parsed with lxml.etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entities are resolved, enabling XML External Entity (XXE) attacks for local file disclosure and SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'name' request parameter is interpolated directly into an XPath expression ".//user[name/text()='%s']" % params["name"]. An attacker can break out of the string literal with a single quote and inject arbitrary XPath predicates to extract all user data, including passwords.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: The 'size' request parameter controls both the repetition count of '#' characters and the range() iteration count with no upper bound. A large value (e.g. size=100000000) allocates enormous strings/lists and exhausts server memory and CPU, causing denial of service.

The 'comment' request parameter is inserted into an SQL statement via string formatting: "INSERT INTO comments VALUES(NULL, '%s', '%s')" % (params["comment"], ...). A comment value containing a single quote can terminate the string literal and inject arbitrary SQL.

Stored comment values are rendered into the HTML table with "%s" without HTML escaping. A malicious comment persisted via the 'comment' parameter is executed as script whenever the comment listing (/?comment=) is viewed, giving stored XSS.

The 'include' request parameter selects a local file or remote URL whose contents are read at line 56 and executed with exec(program, envs) at line 57. An attacker can point 'include' at attacker-controlled content to achieve arbitrary Python code execution (RCE), and also read local files via the file branch.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The 'redir' request parameter is injected unvalidated into a meta refresh tag (content="0; url=%s"). An attacker can craft a link that redirects victims to an arbitrary external site (open redirect), useful for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The 'callback' request parameter is reflected verbatim into the /users.json response as a JSONP wrapper ("%s(" % params["callback"]). Arbitrary JavaScript in the callback value executes in the victim's browser (reflected XSS via JSONP).

The 'password' request parameter is concatenated into the login SQL query without any sanitization (only 'username' is filtered). Supplying a password such as "' OR '1' LIKE '1" bypasses authentication and logs in as an arbitrary user.

The USERS_XML constant hardcodes plaintext account passwords in source code (e.g. admin:7en8aiDoh!, dricci:12345, amason:gandalf, svargas:phest1945). Hardcoded credentials in source are exposed to anyone with repository access.

The 'charset' request parameter is concatenated directly into the Content-Type response header via send_header() without validation. URL-decoded CR/LF characters allow HTTP response splitting / header injection, enabling arbitrary response headers and cache poisoning.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: The response explicitly sets the header X-XSS-Protection: 0, disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter and increasing the impact of the reflected/stored XSS issues in this application.

The SESSIONID cookie is set via a meta Set-Cookie tag with only 'path=/' and without the HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes, allowing it to be read by JavaScript (e.g. via the XSS flaws) and transmitted over plain HTTP.
